panels.title: ⏳ WAITING now
panels.description: Requests queued behind others. Anything above 0 for minutes = users experience a 'hang'. THE health number of this box.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Requests being generated right now (batched together on the GPU).

panels.title: Queue wait p95
panels.description: Seconds requests spent waiting before serving (5m window). Green <5s, red >30s. NOTE: a steady 285ms is the histogram floor (smallest bucket 0.3s) and means NO queueing — only values above 300ms are real measurements.

panels.title: GPU util
panels.description: High is NORMAL under load (the GPU is doing work). Only a problem if WAITING is also red.

panels.title: KV cache
panels.description: Engine memory for active conversations. >90% sustained = preemption thrash.

panels.title: MTP accept
panels.description: Speculative-decoding acceptance. Healthy: 75%+. A drop = free speed lost.

panels.title: 🔔 Alerts firing
panels.description: Prometheus alert rules currently firing (see alerts.yml). Green 0 = all clear.

panels.title: Running vs WAITING
panels.description: The saturation story in one graph. Red (WAITING) above zero = new requests are stuck behind long ones; users say 'it stopped responding'.

panels.title: Queue wait time — p95 & average
panels.description: Seconds spent queued before serving. QUANTIZATION FLOOR: the histogram's smallest bucket is 0.3s, so when every request waits less than that, p95 reads a flat 0.95x0.3 = 285ms — that flat line MEANS 'no queueing'. The avg series has no floor and shows the true small value. Real trouble = p95 climbing past the dashed 5s/30s lines.

panels.title: Time to first token & end-to-end (p95)
panels.description: TTFT = when the answer starts appearing. e2e = full request. Climbing e2e with flat TTFT = longer generations, not congestion.

panels.title: Streaming speed (inter-token p95)
panels.description: Seconds per generated token as users see text stream in. Rises when many requests share the GPU.

panels.title: Token load — the CAUSE of pressure
panels.description: Prompt tok/s = context being ingested (agent transcripts — the saturation driver). Generated tok/s = output. Spikes here precede WAITING.

panels.title: 🛡 Gateway protections — cap, rate limit, who loads the box
Rejections /min (protections firing)
panels.description: Cap 400s: oversized prompts bounced (CLIs auto-compact and retry — occasional ones are HEALTHY). 429s: a key over GATEWAY_RPM_PER_KEY. Sustained spikes fire alerts.

panels.title: Requests /min by model
panels.description: Which model alias carries the traffic (uai-large = local Qwen, claude-opus-4-8 = cloud Anthropic, uai-vision = VLM).

panels.title: Top API keys (req/min now)
panels.description: Requests/min per API key right now (top 10). The in-cell bar is scaled to the 30/min per-key limit — a full red bar is a throttled key. key = first 8 chars of the API key.

panels.title: Top users (req/min now)
panels.description: Requests/min per PERSON behind the shared app-builder key (top 10, from X-UT-Acting-User). The in-cell bar is scaled to the 30/min per-user limit — a full red bar means that user is being throttled.

panels.title: Prompt size at the gate (p95 est. tokens)
panels.description: How close real traffic runs to GATEWAY_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS (red line = 65536, the cap). Hugging the line = users compact often; far below = cap is invisible to them.

panels.title: Gateway HTTP outcomes /min
panels.description: Forwarded requests by status (green 2xx / orange 4xx / red 5xx). Gateway-side rejections live in the panel on the left, not here.

panels.title: Prefill vs decode p95 — which phase eats the GPU
panels.description: Prefill = reading the prompt (compute-bound). Decode = generating (bandwidth-bound). Tells you WHAT kind of load dominates.

panels.title: Prompt size reaching the ENGINE (p95)
panels.description: PROOF the cap holds: must stay under ~65k. Above the red line = something bypasses the gateway (direct :8001 access?).

panels.title: Request outcomes /min
panels.description: stop = clean finish. length = max_tokens hit. RED abort = client gave up waiting (timeout) — the old 'hang' signature.

panels.title: KV cache % & preemptions
panels.description: Preemptions = engine evicting running requests to make memory room (recompute thrash). Should stay at 0.

panels.title: Batch concurrency
panels.description: Requests decoded together. Flat-topping at the same number under load = --max-num-seqs / batched-tokens ceiling.

panels.title: MTP acceptance trend
panels.description: Speculative decoding health over time. 75%+ green = MTP paying for itself. A regression after a model/image swap shows here first.

panels.title: Memory BANDWIDTH — the real decode bottleneck
panels.description: Decode reads all weights per token: THIS pegging near 100% is why generation speed is capped, regardless of FLOPs. GB300 only — the GB10 iGPU has no DCGM profiling (empty there is normal).

panels.title: Compute activity — SM & tensor pipes
panels.description: High tensor + low DRAM = prefill-bound. Low tensor + high DRAM = decode-bound. GB300 only — empty on the GB10 (no DCGM profiling).

panels.title: GPU memory (framebuffer)
panels.description: Device-level memory (GB300: the 256GB HBM3e pool). Empty on the GB10 — unified memory means the HOST memory panel below IS its GPU memory.

panels.title: Temperature & SM clock
panels.description: Clocks dropping while temp climbs = thermal throttling (watch on the GB300 workstation).

panels.title: Utilization & power
panels.description: Power far below TDP at 100% util confirms bandwidth-bound work (the GPU waits on memory, not compute).

panels.title: Host CPU — average & hottest core
panels.description: Hottest core pinned at 100% = EngineCore's conductor loop — NORMAL. Average creeping up = something else on the box.

panels.title: Host memory & disk used %
panels.description: Model weight caches fill disks fast. Red line 90% — the HostDiskLow alert fires at 90%+.

panels.title: Container restarts (last 1h)
panels.description: A single bar = a deploy. A staircase = crash loop. Restarting nim-llm costs minutes of LLM downtime.

panels.title: Scrape targets up (1 = healthy)
panels.description: Every exporter this dashboard depends on. caddy stays down until its Caddyfile enables metrics (see prometheus.yml comment) — expected.

panels.title: Alerts firing over time
panels.description: History of which alert rules fired and when — incident timeline at a glance.
